{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Laura Guggenbühl''' (November 18, 1901 – March 8, 1985) was an American mathematician, one of the earliest women in the U.S. to earn a Ph.D. in mathematics, known for her work in [[triangle geometry]] and the [[history of mathematics]].{{r|pw}}

==Life==
Guggenbühl was born in [[New York City]], to a family of Swiss immigrants; her father, a butcher and baker, died by 1920. She graduated from [[Hunter College]] in 1922 with a bachelor's degree in mathematics, after also taking some classes at [[Columbia University]] and [[New York University]]. She became an instructor at Hunter College while earning a master's degree and Ph.D. from [[Bryn Mawr College]] in 1924 and 1926 respectively.{{r|pw}} Her dissertation, supervised by [[Anna Johnson Pell Wheeler]], was ''An Integral Equation with an Associated Integral Condition''.{{r|mgp}} She became a regular-rank faculty member at Hunter College in 1932 and retired from there as an associate professor in 1972.{{r|pw}}

She died on a round-the-world cruise, shortly after leaving [[Hong Kong]], after being overcome with grief at the recent death of her brother.{{r|pw}}

==Contributions==
Although not active in research mathematics after her doctorate, Guggenbühl represented Hunter College at many offerings of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]]. She
also published several works on the history of mathematics, including biographies of [[Henri Brocard]] and [[Karl Wilhelm Feuerbach]], on elementary geometry including [[triangle geometry]], and on the [[Rhind mathematical papyrus]].{{r|pw}}

==Works==
* 1927: [https://books.google.com/books?id=6mC4AAAAIAAJ An Integral Equation with an Associated Integral Condition] from [[Google Books]]
* 1953: "Henry Brocard and the Geometry of the Triangle", [[Mathematical Gazette]] 37: 241 to 3 {{doi|10.2307/3610034}}
* 1964: "The New York Fragments of the Rhind Mathematical Papyrus", [[The Mathematics Teacher]] 57(6): 406–10 [https://www.jstor.org/stable/27957095?seq=1#page_scan_tab_contents JSTOR]
* 1965: "Mathematics in Ancient Egypt: A checklist (1930 to 1965)", ''The Mathematics Teacher'' 58(7): 630-34 [https://www.jstor.org/stable/27957204?seq=1#page_scan_tab_contents JSTOR]
* 1973: "Rereading Rhind" (book review) [[Isis (journal)|Isis]] 64: 533,4 {{doi|10.1086/351182}}
